answer: Snapshot as of October 3, 2026. (1) September 30, 2026: Cal-Maine reported fiscal Q1 2027 (13 weeks ended August 29, 2026): net sales USD 539.6 million (-41.5% from USD 922.6 million), gross profit USD 0.4 million, operating loss USD 82.2 million and a net loss attributable of USD 58.6 million, or USD 1.26 per diluted share, versus net income of USD 199.3 million (USD 4.12) a year earlier [H20-E1][H20-E3]. Conventional shell egg net sales fell 59.5% on a 59.3% lower average selling price (segment loss USD 71.0 million); Specialty Shell Eggs and Prepared Foods rose to 54.1% of net sales [H20-E1]. (2) Under the variable dividend policy no dividend is payable for the quarter; USD 94.5 million of cumulative loss must be recovered before any future dividend [H20-E1]. (3) Buybacks: 66,601 shares for USD 5.0 million in the quarter (USD 315.7 million left of the USD 500 million program) and 204,888 shares for USD 14.9 million after quarter end [H20-E1]. (4) On August 31, 2026 (8-K filed September 2) the company entered into a Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement: a five-year senior unsecured revolver of up to USD 250 million (accordion up to another USD 250 million), maturing August 31, 2031, with nothing borrowed at September 1 [H20-E2]. Secondary coverage corroborates the loss and dividend decision [H20-E4].

output.answer:
Here is what Cal-Maine Foods (Nasdaq: CALM) reported/disclosed in the 30 days before October 3, 2026 (i.e., Sept. 3 – Oct. 3, 2026). The main event was its fiscal Q1 2027 results on **September 30, 2026**; the financing change dates to the very start of that window.

## Quarterly results — Q1 fiscal 2027 (announced Sept. 30, 2026; 8-K/press release, quarter ended Aug. 29, 2026)

Key figures vs. the prior-year quarter:

| Metric | Q1 FY2027 | Q1 FY2026 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net sales | $539.6M | $922.6M | –41.5% |
| Gross profit | $0.4M | $311.3M | –99.9% |
| Operating income (loss) | $(82.2)M | $249.2M | –133.0% |
| Net income (loss) | $(58.6)M | $199.3M | –129.4% |
| Diluted EPS | $(1.26) | $4.12 | –$5.38 |

Segment operating income: Conventional Shell Eggs $(71.0)M (vs. $168.2M); Specialty Shell Eggs $14.9M (vs. $64.2M); Prepared Foods $7.8M (vs. $13.2M). The loss was driven largely by a ~59% drop in conventional shell egg pricing amid industry oversupply, not volume. Speciality eggs + prepared foods were ~54% of net sales. EPS of –$1.26 missed consensus by about $0.49; revenue missed by ~$22M.

## Shareholder returns

- **Dividend:** No cash dividend declared for Q1 FY2027 under the variable dividend policy. Cumulative loss to be recovered before resuming any dividend: **$94.5M** as of Aug. 29, 2026.
- **Share repurchases:** Repurchased **66,601 shares for $5.0M** during Q1; **$315.7M remained available** under the $500M authorization at quarter-end. Subsequent to quarter-end, repurchased **204,888 shares for $14.9M**.

## Financing

- **Aug. 31, 2026:** Entered into a **Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement** (disclosed in the Sept. 30, 2026 10-Q), replacing the Nov. 15, 2021 facility. It provides a **$250M senior unsecured revolving credit facility** (with an accordion for up to an additional $250M via incremental term loans/increased commitments), **five-year term maturing Aug. 31, 2031**.
- **No borrowings** outstanding under the facility as of Sept. 30, 2026; only **$5.9M in standby letters of credit**. Company reported being **"virtually debt-free"** with **~$767.6M in cash and temporary cash investments** at quarter-end.

Sources:
- https://investors.calmainefoods.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cal-maine-foods-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-results
- https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CALM/8-k-cal-maine-foods-inc-reports-material-event-b4835c83a140.html
- https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CALM/10-q-cal-maine-foods-inc-quarterly-earnings-report-29973a853c98.html
- https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/01/cal-maine-foods-calm-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript
- https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9103118/calmaine-foods-calm-reports-q1-earnings-miss-shares-rise-despite-revenue-decline

No other separate financing, M&A, or capital-return announcements from Cal-Maine appeared in that 30-day window beyond the above.
